## Every published model

The paper's models were fit in Stata, and several of them were never in the original R code: the R file had exploratory models only. This analysis fits every model the paper and its supplement report, as they are presented (decided by Vagish Hemmige, 27 October 2026):

| Table | Blocks | Outcome and exposure |
|---|---|---|
| Table 2 | With and without albumin and hemoglobin; without HSAs with 0 facilities | Early start, density category |
| eTable 1 | Black and White individuals | Early start, density category |
| eTable 2 | With and without albumin and hemoglobin; albumin and hemoglobin multiply imputed; Black and White individuals | Early start, continuous density |
| eTable 3 | With albumin and hemoglobin; without HSAs with 0 facilities | eGFR (linear), density category |

Each block has Models 1 to 3. The models are listed in one table, one row per published column, so nothing reported is missed and a model that appears in two blocks (Model 1 in both blocks of Table 2) is fit once. Model 1 never includes albumin or hemoglobin and uses all patients of its group, as in Table 2, where it is identical in both blocks. Within a race group, race is not a covariate. The eTable 1 headings disagree on whether albumin and hemoglobin are included (see the [supplement](supplement.qmd)); both of its sample sizes match the complete-case models, so they are included.

```{r}
#| label: define-published-models
#| eval: false
```

## Models

Mixed-effects models with a random intercept for HSA, progressively adjusted, fit with [{glmmTMB}](https://glmmtmb.github.io/glmmTMB/) [@glmmtmb]: logistic for early start, linear for eGFR. With albumin and hemoglobin, patients missing either value drop out of Models 2 and 3, as in the paper's complete-case models. The covariates follow the paper's Table 2 footnotes; the "HSA quality benchmarks" in Model 3 are taken to be the three the paper's Methods give as examples ("such as": HbA1c testing and eye examinations among enrollees with diabetes, and ambulatory-sensitive discharges).

### Choosing the model-fitting package

The analysis uses {glmmTMB} rather than [{lme4}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=lme4) or Stata itself (decided by Vagish Hemmige, 27 October 2026); why is on [How the models are fitted](study_analysis.qmd#how-the-models-are-fitted). The comparison was run on synthetic test data shaped like Model 3 (4,000 patients, 60 HSAs, about 40 covariate terms), they compared as follows:

| Fit (synthetic test data) | Time | Convergence warnings | Odds ratio, highest vs zero density (synthetic) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lme4::glmer` [@lme4_pkg], default settings | 117 s | 4 | 10.08 (not converged) |
| `lme4::glmer`, rescaled covariates, higher iteration limit | 111 s | 0 | 10.62 |
| `lme4::glmer`, 7-point quadrature (Stata's default) | 119 s | 0 | 10.63 |
| {glmmTMB} [@glmmtmb] | 4 s | 0 | 10.63 |

The figures are from synthetic test data, not from USRDS data, and say nothing about the study's results; only the comparison between rows matters. {glmmTMB} gave the same estimates as a fully converged `glmer` in about a thirtieth of the time, without rescaling, and quadrature with 7 points rather than the Laplace approximation changed the odds ratios only in the third decimal, because each synthetic HSA has many patients (about 67).

## Multiple imputation

Only albumin and hemoglobin are imputed, 10 times, by predictive mean matching (the [{mice}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=mice) default for numeric variables [@vanbuuren2011mice]), from the outcome, the density category and the Model 3 covariates, without HSA or continuous density as predictors (decision D7). How this reads the paper's description is on [Missing laboratory values](study_analysis.qmd#missing-laboratory-values).

## Fitting

Each distinct model is fit once and its density terms extracted: odds ratios for the logistic models, differences in eGFR for eTable 3, each with a 95% Wald confidence interval. Imputed models are fit on each completed data set and pooled by Rubin's rules [@rubin1987mi], whose intervals combine the variation within and between the imputed data sets. Each model reports the number of patients it used. For the imputed models this is the number each completed data set's fit used, which is the same in every one, because only albumin and hemoglobin are imputed and a patient missing another covariate is dropped from all of them; the run stops if the numbers differ.

**Functions used:** [`density_effects()`](functions.qmd#density-effects), [`mixed_formula()`](functions.qmd#model-formulas).

```{r}
#| label: fit-published-models
#| eval: false
```

### One model written out

The code above builds every model from the list rather than writing each one out, so no single model appears in it. As an example, this is what it fits for Table 2, Model 3, with albumin and hemoglobin, the paper's fully adjusted model. Each row of the list becomes a call like this one; the other models drop or add covariates, change the patients, or swap the outcome or exposure.

```r
# Table 2, block "With albumin and hemoglobin", Model 3:
# outcome early_start, exposure density_category, patients "All", labs TRUE
fit <- glmmTMB(
  early_start ~ density_category +
    # Model 1: demographics and year (model_1_covariates)
    age + sex + race + hispanic + dialysis_year +
    # Model 2 adds comorbidities, access and cause (model_2_covariates)
    heart_failure + coronary_disease + diabetes + cerebrovascular_disease +
    alcohol_or_drug + immobility + institutionalized + access_type + esrd_cause +
    # Model 3 adds insurance, nephrology care and area measures (model_3_covariates)
    insurance + nephrology_care + rural_urban + zip_percent_poverty +
    zip_percent_black + hsa_ambulatory_sensitive_discharges +
    hsa_percent_eye_exam + hsa_percent_hba1c +
    # labs = TRUE adds the laboratory values (model_2_laboratory)
    albumin + hemoglobin +
    # random intercept for HSA
    (1 | hsanum),
  data = patient_groups[["All"]],   # model_data: the whole cohort
  family = binomial
)

# The rows reported: odds ratios for the four density categories against
# HSAs with no facility, with 95% CIs, p values and the patients used
density_effects(fit, "^density_category", exponentiate = TRUE)
```

In the code, `model_covariates("Model 3", labs = TRUE, patients = "All")` returns these 24 covariates, and `mixed_formula()` turns them into the formula. A test (`tests/test-model-example.R`) checks that the formula on this page is the one the code builds, so the example cannot drift from the code.

## Variance decomposition

How much of the variation in eGFR at initiation lies between HSAs, and between facilities within HSAs, from two null linear mixed models fit by `lme4::lmer` with its default, restricted maximum likelihood (REML). Both models are fit on the patients with a dialysis facility ID, which the nested model needs; see [Variation between and within HSAs](study_analysis.qmd#variation-between-and-within-hsas).

## Saving

Estimates are saved in the gitignored `models/` folder, so tables can be rebuilt without refitting. With them are saved the version of each package in `provenance_packages` (set in `setup.R`), and for [{usRds}](https://vagishhemmige.github.io/usRds/), which is installed from GitHub while its facility functions are unreleased, the repository and commit. A result can then be traced to the code that produced it, which matters while {usRds} is changing ([{usRds} issue #18](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/usRds/issues/18)).

**Functions used:** [`package_provenance()`](functions.qmd#package-provenance).
